name: Karura Forest Waterfall Loop
bestSeason: Year-round. Trails are driest and least muddy in January to March and June to October.
summary: A shaded loop through one of the largest urban forests in the world, with a waterfall, a bamboo grove and a historic cave. Wide, well-signed paths make it the easiest way to get started.
highlights: Waterfall on the Karura River
Bamboo forest corridor
Cave with Mau Mau history
Birdlife along the river, including turacos and hornbills
bring: Rain jacket in the wet months
Cash or mobile money for entry
tips: Stay on the marked paths and carry your entry receipt. The forest gates close in the evening, so plan to finish well before dusk.
imageAlt: Illustration of tall forest trees in layers of blue-green with a gold sun rising behind them.

name: Oloolua Nature Trail
bestSeason: Year-round. Choose a dry day, because the steps and stream crossings get slippery after rain.
summary: A short forest walk in Karen that follows a stream down to a cave. It is a good first outing for families and for anyone testing new boots.
highlights: Cave at the end of the forest path
Stream crossings and wooden steps
Monkeys and forest birds close to the path
Quiet picnic spots
tips: Go in the morning for the best birdwatching. Take care on the steps near the cave, which stay damp.
imageAlt: Illustration of a forest slope with pine-shaped trees in deep green under a pale morning sky.

name: Ngong Hills Ridge Trail
bestSeason: January to February and June to October, when the ridge is dry and the Rift Valley views are clear.
summary: A ridge walk over a line of rounded peaks with the Rift Valley on one side and the Nairobi skyline on the other. Expect steady ups and downs and strong wind on the tops.
highlights: Sweeping views over the Rift Valley and Nairobi
Wind turbines along the ridge line
Open grassland with grazing cattle and Maasai herders
Sunrise starts that finish before midday
tips: Go in a group and ask the forest guards at the gate about the current escort arrangements. Start early, because the ridge has little shade and the wind picks up by midday.
imageAlt: Illustration of a long ridge of rounded green hills under a rising gold sun with a small hiker on the crest.

name: Hell's Gate Gorge Walk
bestSeason: January to February and June to October. Avoid the gorge after heavy rain because it can flash flood.
summary: A walk between red cliff walls and past volcanic towers in a park where you can hike among zebra, giraffe and buffalo. A short scramble in the narrow section adds some fun.
highlights: Narrow gorge with red and orange rock walls
Fischer's Tower and Central Tower
Wildlife on foot, because the park has few large predators
Natural hot springs near the gorge
tips: Hire a local guide at the gate, who will show you the safe route through the narrow section. Check the weather before you enter, and leave the gorge at once if rain starts upstream.
imageAlt: Illustration of a narrow gorge with warm clay-coloured cliff walls and a tall rock tower in the middle.

name: Mount Longonot Crater Rim
bestSeason: January to February and June to October. The loose scree is easier to climb when dry.
summary: A steep climb up a volcano to a crater rim loop with a forested crater floor below you and Lake Naivasha in the distance. The final section is loose and exposed.
highlights: Full loop around the crater rim at about 2,776 metres
Forest growing on the crater floor
Views of Lake Naivasha and the Rift Valley
Buffalo, zebra and giraffe near the base
tips: Start by 8 am so you finish before the afternoon heat. The rim path has steep drops on the crater side, so keep to the path and avoid walking in strong wind.
imageAlt: Illustration of a volcano with a crater notch at its peak above a pale lake and acacia trees.

name: Crescent Island Walking Safari
bestSeason: January to February and June to October, when the island is dry and the grass is short.
summary: A flat walk around a crescent-shaped island on Lake Naivasha where giraffe, zebra, waterbuck and wildebeest graze close to the path. A short boat ride takes you there.
highlights: Close views of grazing giraffe and zebra
Flat paths that suit all ages
Boat transfer across Lake Naivasha
Fish eagles and pelicans around the shore
tips: Walk slowly and keep your distance from the animals. Book the boat transfer in advance in the busy holiday months.
imageAlt: Illustration of a flat island in a still blue lake with an acacia tree and birds flying overhead.

name: Mount Suswa Crater and Caves
bestSeason: January to February and June to October. The tracks to the crater are rough and slippery in the rains.
summary: A hike into a double crater with a hidden inner plateau and lava-tube caves. The community-run conservancy offers guided walks and camping.
highlights: Crater within a crater with a forested inner plateau
Lava-tube caves with bats
Steam vents on the crater floor
Maasai community guides
bring: Helmet if you plan to enter the caves
tips: Only enter the caves with a local guide, because the rock is uneven and the tunnels are completely dark. Arrange the visit through the conservancy before you travel.
imageAlt: Illustration of a wide crater rim with a dark inner bowl and thin plumes of steam rising.

name: Ol Donyo Sabuk Summit Trail
bestSeason: January to February and June to October, when the summit has clear views.
summary: A forest climb to a summit also known as Kilimambogo, with a park full of baboons and buffalo. The top rewards you with open views across the plains.
highlights: Forest trail through the national park
Baboons, buffalo and colobus monkeys
Historic memorial near the summit
Wide views over the plains toward Thika
tips: Keep food out of sight, because baboons will grab bags. Do not approach buffalo on the path and wait for them to move on.
imageAlt: Illustration of a rounded green mountain rising above plains with scattered trees.

name: Menengai Crater Rim Walk
bestSeason: January to February and June to October. The rim is exposed and misty in the long rains.
summary: A walk along the rim of one of the largest volcanic calderas in the world, with Nakuru town and its lake laid out below. The crater floor is a sea of old lava.
highlights: Rim views over the caldera and Nakuru town
Old lava flows on the crater floor
Steam rising from geothermal vents nearby
Local guides who share the crater's history
tips: Use a local guide from the community group at the gate. Keep well back from the crater edge, especially in mist or wind.
imageAlt: Illustration of a broad caldera rim with a dark crater floor and a warm sky behind it.

name: Eburru Forest Summit
bestSeason: January to February and June to October. The forest tracks are muddy and slippery in the rains.
summary: A long climb through indigenous forest to the highest point of a volcanic massif north-west of Lake Naivasha. Natural steam vents along the route make it feel unlike any other hill in the Rift.
highlights: Cool, shaded indigenous forest
Natural steam vents beside the path
Views across to Lake Naivasha and Lake Elmenteita
Rich birdlife in the forest canopy
tips: Walk with a local guide, since paths branch often and are not signed. Tell someone your route and expected return time.
imageAlt: Illustration of a forested mountain with thin plumes of steam rising from its slope.

name: Mount Kenya: Sirimon to Point Lenana
bestSeason: January to February and August to September, the two driest periods on the mountain.
summary: A four-day trek up the north-west side of Kenya's highest mountain to Point Lenana at 4,985 metres. The route climbs through forest and moorland, then crosses high alpine valleys beneath the main peaks.
highlights: Sunrise from Point Lenana at 4,985 metres
Giant groundsel and lobelia in the moorland
Mackinder's Valley beneath Batian and Nelion
Descent via the Naro Moru route
tips: Climb slowly and allow time to acclimatise, because altitude sickness can affect fit people. A licensed guide is strongly recommended, and park fees and bookings must be arranged in advance. Lenana is a trekking peak, while Batian and Nelion need technical climbing skills.
imageAlt: Illustration of jagged snow-capped peaks above moorland under a pale gold dawn sky.

name: Mount Kenya: Chogoria Route
bestSeason: January to February and August to September, when the high valleys are clearest.
summary: A scenic route up the eastern side of Mount Kenya past mountain lakes and the deep Gorges Valley. Many trekkers rate it the most beautiful way to reach Point Lenana.
highlights: Lake Ellis and Lake Michaelson
Gorges Valley with steep rock walls
Hall Tarns and high moorland
Point Lenana summit at sunrise
tips: Plan your itinerary so you gain height gradually and sleep lower than your highest point when possible. Go with a licensed guide and book park access in advance.
imageAlt: Illustration of a deep mountain valley with a small lake below jagged snow-capped peaks.

name: Mount Elgon: Sasa Trail to Koitoboss
bestSeason: December to March, the driest months on this side of the mountain.
summary: A three-day trek through bamboo and moorland to the caldera rim of an extinct volcano on the Kenya and Uganda border. The summit area is wide, quiet and rarely crowded.
highlights: Koitoboss peak at about 4,187 metres
Hot springs inside the caldera
Bamboo forest and afro-alpine moorland
Far fewer trekkers than Mount Kenya
tips: Arrange a ranger or guide through the park before you set out. The trek is long, so build in time to acclimatise and carry enough food for the full route.
imageAlt: Illustration of a wide caldera with steaming hot springs under high rounded peaks.

name: Kerio Valley Escarpment Trail
bestSeason: January to February and June to September. The valley floor is very hot, so start at first light.
summary: A steep trail down from the Elgeyo Escarpment into the Kerio Valley, followed by a hard climb back out. Iten sits at about 2,400 metres, so even fit hikers feel the altitude.
highlights: View Point over the Kerio Valley at the cliff edge
Sweeping views of the escarpment wall
Training paths used by long-distance runners
Farming villages and fig trees on the slopes
tips: Save your energy for the climb out. Leave the valley floor before the midday heat and keep well back from the cliff edge at the View Point.
imageAlt: Illustration of a high cliff edge looking over a hazy valley in layers of blue and gold.

name: Kakamega Forest Birding Trails
bestSeason: December to February and June to August, the drier months. Rain can fall at any time in this rainforest.
summary: Gentle walks through Kenya's last remnant of the Guineo-Congolian rainforest, famous for birds and primates. A pre-dawn climb to Lirhanda Hill gives a sunrise over the canopy.
highlights: Great blue turaco and many other forest birds
Red-tailed monkeys and black-and-white colobus
Sunrise from Lirhanda Hill
Giant forest trees and butterflies
tips: Hire a local birding guide who knows where the species live. Walk quietly and early, since activity drops by midday.
imageAlt: Illustration of dense rainforest canopy in many greens with a bird flying across the sky.

name: Taita Hills: Vuria Peak
bestSeason: January to February and June to October, when clouds clear from the summit.
summary: A climb through cloud forest to the highest point of the Taita Hills at about 2,208 metres. The hills belong to the Eastern Arc Mountains and hold birds found nowhere else.
highlights: Summit views toward Tsavo and Mount Kilimanjaro on clear days
Endemic birds, including the Taita thrush and Taita apalis
Cloud forest patches and small farms
Cool air after the hot Tsavo road
tips: Hire a local guide from Wundanyi, who knows the forest patches and the best birding spots. Start early because cloud often covers the top by midday.
imageAlt: Illustration of steep green hills with low cloud drifting through the valleys below a pale sky.
